situation:
You are the district manager for CEDAR MILL BOWLS, a fast-casual bowl company with nine restaurants. The company is profitable, and its founder (judge) is preparing to sell it and step away next year. The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend how the restaurants should cover the work that has to be done after the doors close at night.

Each restaurant closes at nine. Four crew members stay about ninety minutes afterward to break down the hot wells, clean the line and mop the floor. Those hours sit in a labor budget that is fixed for the year, and the founder (judge) has ruled out raising bowl prices to pay for them after the last increase cost the company dinner traffic.

The closing crew is mostly students who take the late hours because they cannot work during the day. The mid-afternoon shift between two and five is worked by the long-tenured full-time crew, and it is the slowest stretch of the day; the dining room is often close to empty while three people stand behind the line.

Cutting the closing crew from four to two moves the cleaning into the last hour the dining room is open. The two students who lose those shifts lose about eight paid hours a week, and evening customers eat while the line is broken down and the floor is mopped. Paying for four closers out of the slow mid-afternoon shift protects the students, and the afternoon crew lose hours they count on.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on how the closing work should be covered, and on what you would say to the crew who lose hours. You will present in the office at the flagship restaurant. The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the founder's questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of CEDAR MILL BOWLS, preparing to sell the company and step away next year. Business background is the same as the situation above. You want the district manager to recommend how the closing work gets covered inside the labor budget, and to tell you plainly what the crew who lose hours will be told.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: Who loses the most under your recommendation?
What do you say to that person when they ask why?
